summary: Client-side CHOP for synchronizing timelines across multiple TouchDesigner processes with a Sync Out CHOP server.
key_concepts: Sync In CHOP participates in a TouchDesigner Pro Sync In/Sync Out pair that keeps timelines in multiple processes within a single frame.
A sync setup uses one Sync Out process and one or more Sync In client processes.
Sync In client processes should run with Realtime off because their frame rate is determined by the Sync Out CHOP.
Sync CHOPs synchronize by pausing their own timelines until the participating Sync In/Out CHOPs have cooked.
If any Sync process fails to communicate, the other processes time out and may all run slowly.
Extra CHOP channels sent through Sync Out are received by Sync In clients, making the pair useful for frame sync plus small synchronized control values.

key_params.name: multicastaddress
key_params.note: Multicast address used to discover/synchronize with Sync Out

key_params.name: port
key_params.note: Network port shared with Sync Out

common_gotchas: Official Sync In page returned a Derivative MediaWiki database error during 2026-06-19 verification; shared behavior was verified from the official Sync Out page.
Official docs list the Sync pair as TouchDesigner Pro only.
Client processes with Sync In should have the Realtime flag off because Sync Out determines their frame rates.
All monitors across server and clients should use the same refresh rate.
If any Sync process fails to communicate, the others can timeout and all processes may run slowly.
Windows firewall can block communication; check firewall before blaming network logic.
